Let me analyze this conflict.

Axis: applicant
- Register: "ESIT Elektronik Sistemler Imalat ve Ticaret Limited Sirketi"
- Document: "Esit Elektronik Ltd. Sti."

These are Turkish company names. "ESIT Elektronik Sistemler Imalat ve Ticaret Limited Sirketi" translates to "Esit Electronic Systems Manufacturing and Trading Limited Company". "Esit Elektronik Ltd. Sti." is the abbreviated form: "Esit Elektronik Limited Şirketi" — "Ltd. Sti." is the common Turkish abbreviation for "Limited Şirketi" (limited company).

So the document's name is a shortened/abbreviated form of the full legal name in the register. The core identifying element "Esit Elektronik" is the same. "Ltd. Sti." = "Limited Sirketi". The difference is:
- Capitalization drift (ESIT vs Esit)
- The register includes "Sistemler Imalat ve Ticaret" (systems manufacturing and trade) which the document omits
- "Limited Sirketi" vs "Ltd. Sti." — same suffix, abbreviated

According to the rules: "spelling drift, legal-suffix drift, accent differences = same-entity."

Is omission of the middle words just drift, or a genuinely different name? This is clearly the same company — ESIT Elektronik is a known Turkish company (weighing instruments manufacturer, hence R134 load cells certificate). The abbreviated trade name "Esit Elektronik Ltd. Sti." is the same entity as the full legal name.

So verdict: same-entity.

Best value: For same-entity, the rules say for number/year format differences use register's canonical form. For spelling drift, it says same-entity but doesn't explicitly say which value. Hmm. Let me re-read: "spelling drift, legal-suffix drift, accent differences = same-entity." It doesn't specify best_value for this case explicitly, except for number/year formats (register's canonical form) and document-noise (register) and different-entity (document).

The general principle: the register is the OIML-CS database, the certificate is the legal instrument. For a name conflict that's merely abbreviation/drift, the fuller legal name in the register is more canonical and complete. The register's value "ESIT Elektronik Sistemler Imalat ve Ticaret Limited Sirketi" is the full expanded legal name, which is the better canonical form for a fused record. The document's "Esit Elektronik Ltd. Sti." is an abbreviation.

So best_value = register's form: "ESIT Elektronik Sistemler Imalat ve Ticaret Limited Sirketi".

Verdict: same-entity. Why: document is an abbreviated form of the same Turkish company (Ltd. Sti. = Limited Sirketi), so register's full legal name is canonical.
